method.scale_intro: Each harm is scored out of 100. Heritage counts for most of the score. Full marks require separately identifying people of European descent, not only a broader category such as White, or a proxy such as nationality.
method.cap_applied_body: The uncapped total is {uncapped}%. A country with no real ethnicity data is capped at 25%.
method.previous: On the previous rubric this country scored {score}%.
method.previous_with_band: On the previous rubric this country scored {score}% ({band}).
method.previous_weights: Harm weights changed on {date}. With the earlier weights (sexual abuse 25%, the other five harms 15% each) this country scored {score}%.
method.colours: Map colours: {bands}. Scores are reviewed as new data is found (last review {date}).
method.gold: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies people of European descent, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when European-descent children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm.
method.cap: Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most one quarter of the heritage points. A country with no real ethnicity data is capped at 25%, however complete its other counting is.
method.weights: The country score is a weighted average of the six harms: homicide 25%, sexual abuse 20%, sex trafficking 20%, physical abuse 15%, online exploitation 10% and neglect 10% (weights in use since 19 November 2026).
method.comp_victim_full: Published by harm, with people of European descent identified separately — not only a broader category such as White, or a proxy such as nationality.
method.comp_other_full: Broad coverage, a low share of unknowns, rates per 100,000, victim–perpetrator linkage, and public, timely release.
